purpose: Bounded visual transcription of the Karlsruhe elements/complexion passage under the physician rubric through the next red section heading; no Voynich materials accessed.

karlsruhe_platform_91v.provenance: Official institution-served image rendition, inspected natively. Six short prose lines follow the rubric to the right of the physician, and six lines continue below the image.

karlsruhe_platform_92r.provenance: Official institution-served image rendition, inspected natively. Counted 21 prose baselines before the next red rubric, Die erste complexion Sanguinea.

augsburg_1491_scan_00172.use: Separate printed witness consulted as a reading/context aid. Its verse after the doctor-and-flask image says the year has four kinds of nature according to its state and that bodies likewise change their natures. It was not used to fill missing Karlsruhe readings.

augsburg_1491_scan_00176.use: Separate print witness inspected as parallel context. It explicitly lists bodily materials alongside elements, including water/blood/moisture and earth/flesh/bone. Not used to silently restore Karlsruhe text.

augsburg_1491_scan_00171.use: Adjacent preceding scan checked only to locate the same chapter sequence and the transition to the following illustrated passage.

legacy_pointer.use: Located the official 1491 HAB scan sequence. The legacy pointer was read-only; its frozen files were not changed.

transcription_scope.method: Visual reading from the official institution-served images; no OCR. Original spelling is retained selectively. Square brackets flag uncertain or unreadable letters/words.

correction_history.reason: The visible line is an element/body-material sequence; the earlier reading mistook strokes for blüet/am frühling. Do not retain spring/flowering semantics.

limits: Not every line supports a complete reading; uncertain and unreadable lines remain marked rather than silently filled.
The Karlsruhe manuscript's complete element/body list and any season mapping were not established from this bounded reading.
The Augsburg print is a distinct witness, not a surrogate transcript of the Karlsruhe copy.
Catalog descriptions are not used as manuscript transcriptions.
